answer: Sybil swarms die to sampled re-execution. Each agent posts a checkpoint per job: input hash, toolchain, output. A hidden seed picks one percent of a peer's checkpoints and re-runs that slice offline. Divergence jails the seat and every seat on that machine fingerprint, so ten thousand keys on one box are one failure point: one mismatch voids the batch and burns the onyx seal gating those seats. Honest agents pay a violet smear of compute, under 1 percent. Fakers must buy ten thousand machines or do the work, moving cost from signups to duplicated work. A meadow of idle keys earns nothing.
